title: UNTIL Inclusive Bound, Value Type Alignment, and UTC/Floating Timezone Alignment with DTSTART

citations.verbatim_quote: The UNTIL rule part defines a DATE or DATE-TIME value that bounds the recurrence rule in an inclusive manner. If the value specified by UNTIL is synchronized with the specified recurrence, this DATE or DATE-TIME becomes the last instance of the recurrence. The value of the UNTIL rule part MUST have the same value type as the "DTSTART" property. Furthermore, if the "DTSTART" property is specified as a date with local time, then the UNTIL rule part MUST also be specified as a date with local time. If the "DTSTART" property is specified as a date with UTC time or a date with local time and time zone reference, then the UNTIL rule part MUST be specified as a date with UTC time.

If an object is split to make a "this and future" change to a recurrence, the original object MUST be truncated to end at the previous occurrence before this split, and a new object is created to represent all the occurrences after the split.

rationale: For recurring calendar components (VEVENT, VTODO, and VJOURNAL; whereas VTIMEZONE STANDARD and DAYLIGHT sub-components always require UTC UNTIL values per RFC 5545 Section 3.3.10), RFC 5545 Section 3.3.10 mandates three invariants for any RRULE UNTIL bound (enforced as RFC_5545 invariant I-C-007): (1) UNTIL is an inclusive upper bound (if UNTIL equals a generated occurrence instant, that occurrence is included as the final instance). (2) UNTIL MUST have the same value type (DATE vs DATE-TIME) as DTSTART. (3) When DTSTART is a DATE-TIME, if DTSTART is floating local time (Form #1), UNTIL MUST also be floating local time; if DTSTART is UTC (Form #2) or local time with a TZID parameter (Form #3), UNTIL MUST be formatted in UTC ('Z'). However, RFC 5545 and RFC 8984 Section 4.1.3 allow multiple equivalent encodings when truncating a series before a split target (for example, setting UNTIL to the exact previous occurrence timestamp or adjusting COUNT). Choosing specifically to replace COUNT with `UNTIL = split_instant - 1 second` (`split_date - 1 day` for DATE) is a STORE_POLICY encoding choice that satisfies all RFC 5545 Section 3.3.10 invariants without computing the prior occurrence instant.
store_implication: Component validation MUST enforce RFC 5545 Section 3.3.10's UNTIL value-type and UTC/floating alignment with DTSTART (invariant I-C-007). In addition, by STORE_POLICY, store operations that truncate RRULE.UNTIL for THIS_AND_FUTURE deletion or series splitting clear COUNT and set UNTIL as follows: (1) For a DATE DTSTART, set UNTIL to `target_date - 1 day`. (2) For a floating DATE-TIME DTSTART, set UNTIL to `target_dt - 1 second`. (3) For a UTC or TZID-qualified DATE-TIME DTSTART, align the split occurrence time to DTSTART's timezone, convert to UTC, and set UNTIL to `target_utc - 1 second` (not 1 day) so UNTIL is a UTC DATE-TIME that excludes the split occurrence and all later occurrences while inclusively retaining all prior occurrences across DST transitions and sub-daily frequencies.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Timezone-aware DTSTART (e.g. TZID=America/New_York) paired with a floating UNTIL (e.g. UNTIL=20250505T090000 without 'Z'): violates RFC 5545 Section 3.3.10 and must be rejected or normalized to UTC.

Spring-forward DST transition on a TZID-aware daily series (e.g. America/New_York 2025-03-08 09:00 EST = 14:00Z, 2025-03-09 09:00 EDT = 13:00Z): subtracting 1 day in UTC from 2025-03-09T13:00:00Z yields 2025-03-08T13:00:00Z, which is 1 hour before the March 8 occurrence (14:00Z) and falsely excludes March 8; subtracting 1 second (2025-03-09T12:59:59Z) preserves March 8.

Sub-daily frequency (e.g. FREQ=HOURLY at 09:00, 10:00, 11:00): subtracting 1 day when truncating THISANDFUTURE at 11:00 sets UNTIL to the previous day and falsely excludes the 09:00 and 10:00 instances on the same day.

scenarios.name: this_and_future_delete_tzid_series_sets_utc_until
scenarios.description: Deleting THISANDFUTURE on a TZID-aware daily series aligns the target recurrence_id to DTSTART's timezone, converts to UTC, and sets an inclusive UTC UNTIL bound that retains prior occurrences across DST transitions.
